findings.entity: reflected man vs. real man (mirror viewpoint geometry)
findings.description: The camera sees the real man in roughly 3/4 rear view (back of head, right ear and right jawline visible, face turned away toward the mirror), which for a planar mirror facing the camera implies the reflection should show his face from a strongly oblique front-right angle. Instead the reflection shows an almost fully frontal face and squared-on torso looking toward the lens throughout the clip (clearest at 01.75 and 03.25). The real and reflected bodies are not geometrically compatible views of the same person in one plane mirror.

From 02.25 to 04.00 the real right hand is raised to the crown/back-top of the head with the razor lying against the hair behind the hairline, while the reflected hand is in front of the face with the razor drawn horizontally across the center of the forehead. Similar offsets at 00.00 (real razor under the chin vs. reflected razor at the upper lip) and 01.75 (real razor at the temple above eye level vs. reflected razor on the nose bridge). The reflected hand position does not correspond to where the real hand is in 3D.
